summary: Configured node1 (OPNsense) as the router between lan-a (10.60.1.0/24, vtnet1/opt1, peer node2) and lan-b (10.60.2.0/24, vtnet2/opt2, peer node3). Added pf rules on both opt interfaces that block+log TCP/23 in either direction while passing all other traffic, and confirmed logged block entries in /var/log/filter/ for attempts from node2 and node3. All three nodes were restarted one at a time using native reboot mechanisms; boot identities changed on each and the block+log behavior plus general inter-LAN routing (ping) were re-verified after every restart.
actions_performed: Identified node1 as OPNsense/FreeBSD router with unconfigured vtnet1/vtnet2; node2/node3 as RHEL9 hosts with unconfigured enp8s0 second NICs
Added opt1 (vtnet1, 10.60.1.1/24) and opt2 (vtnet2, 10.60.2.1/24) interfaces to /conf/config.xml on node1 and reconfigured them via configctl

Assigned static IPs to node2 enp8s0 (10.60.1.2/24, via nmcli persistent profile lan-a) and node3 enp8s0 (10.60.2.2/24, via nmcli persistent profile lan-b), with static routes to the other LAN via node1
Confirmed via ARP table that node2 is on opt1/lan-a and node3 is on opt2/lan-b
Added pf filter rules in config.xml: block+log TCP port 23 on opt1 and opt2, plus pass-all rules for other traffic on each; applied with configctl filter reload
Verified telnet(23) connection attempts from node2->node3 and node3->node2 both time out (dropped) and are logged in /var/log/filter/filter_20260905.log with block action and the telnet rule label
Verified normal traffic (ICMP) still routes correctly between lan-a and lan-b
Captured pre-restart boot identity baselines (kern.boottime on node1, /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id on node2/node3) and healthy state

Restarted node1 via 'shutdown -r now', polled until SSH returned, confirmed new kern.boottime, confirmed config.xml-derived interfaces/pf rules persisted, re-verified ping success and telnet block+log
Restarted node2 via 'systemctl reboot', polled until reachable, confirmed new boot_id, confirmed nmcli network profile persisted, re-verified ping and telnet block

Restarted node3 via 'systemctl reboot', polled until reachable, confirmed new boot_id, confirmed nmcli network profile persisted, re-verified ping and telnet block, and captured a fresh log entry for a node3-origin refused telnet attempt

evidence.requirement: node1 routes between lan-a and lan-b
evidence.summary: node2 (lan-a, 10.60.1.2) and node3 (lan-b, 10.60.2.2) configured on separate subnets behind node1's opt1/opt2 interfaces; cross-LAN ping succeeds through node1.

evidence.requirement: Refuse TCP port 23 between the two networks
evidence.summary: pf block rules for tcp/23 added on opt1 and opt2 and confirmed active in the ruleset; connection attempts on port 23 from node2->node3 and node3->node2 both time out (blocked).

evidence.requirement: Record every refused attempt in a log on node1
evidence.summary: filterlog entries in /var/log/filter/filter_20260905.log show 'block' action with the telnet rule label for both directions of blocked port-23 traffic.

evidence.requirement: Show a log entry produced by an attempt made from node2
evidence.summary: Log line: src 10.60.1.2 (node2) -> dst 10.60.2.2 (node3) port 23, action=block, matching the telnet block rule label 78176ca0c89f923b82051ce4f25554fa on vtnet1.
Captured kern.boottime on node1 (sec=1788629261) and boot_id on node2 (377b5195...) and node3 (583ddd53...) plus healthy interface/route state prior to any restart.

evidence.requirement: node1 restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovery
evidence.summary: Reboot acknowledged, node became unreachable, then returned with new kern.boottime (1788629665); opt1/opt2 interfaces and pf telnet-block rules persisted from config.xml; post-reboot ping succeeded and a new blocked/logged telnet attempt from node2 was captured.

evidence.requirement: node2 restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovery
evidence.summary: Reboot acknowledged, node unreachable, then returned with new boot_id (a2597d9a... vs 377b5195...); nmcli lan-a profile reapplied enp8s0 IP/route automatically; post-reboot ping to node3 succeeded and telnet to node3 still blocked.

evidence.requirement: node3 restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovery
evidence.summary: Reboot acknowledged, node unreachable, then returned with new boot_id (c043a424... vs 583ddd53...); nmcli lan-b profile reapplied enp8s0 IP/route automatically; post-reboot ping to node2 succeeded, telnet to node2 blocked, and a fresh logged block entry for the node3-origin attempt was captured on node1.
